seeds.scene: Five tinted acrylic sheets stacked on a printed page; each sheet's individual tint is shown beside the stack. Stack order top→bottom: clear, yellow, cyan, magenta, clear.
seeds.question: What COLOR does the printed text appear when viewed through the full stack?
seeds.lever: Subtractive filtering: yellow blocks blue, cyan blocks red, magenta blocks green → all visible wavelengths blocked → text reads against near-black field.

seeds.scene: A wooden plank shelf supports 4 boxes sitting on it; the plank visibly bows downward beneath box C the most, then under box A, then B, with no bow under D.
seeds.question: Order the boxes from HEAVIEST to LIGHTEST.
seeds.lever: Map plank deflection magnitude to load weight; rank by visible sag amount, treat zero-sag as lightest.

seeds.scene: Six watercolor sheets clipped to a drying rack; each shows a different curl: flat, slight cup, deep cup, tube curl, slight wave, mostly flat with curled corners. A hygrometer-card chart on the wall maps curl shape to humidity ranges.
seeds.question: Which sheet was painted under the LOWEST humidity?
seeds.lever: Tighter curl = larger moisture differential between sides → lowest ambient humidity at painting time; pick the most extreme curl.

seeds.scene: Six pillows on a bed; each shows a hand-print indent from the same shopper. Indent depths and rebound times: P1 deep slow rebound, P2 shallow instant rebound, P3 medium quick rebound, P4 deep quick rebound, P5 no indent, P6 medium slow rebound. A sign requests 'memory foam (deep + slow rebound) for the guest room.'
seeds.question: Which pillow matches the sign's request?
seeds.lever: Memory foam = both deep indent AND slow rebound; P4 is deep but fast (latex), P6 slow but only medium → only P1 satisfies both.

seeds.scene: Four steaks cross-sectioned side by side on a cutting board. S1 cool red center, S2 warm pink center with thin gray band, S3 mostly gray throughout with a thin pink core, S4 fully gray-brown throughout. A printed doneness card maps colors: rare, medium-rare, medium, medium-well, well-done.
seeds.question: Which steak is MEDIUM-WELL?
seeds.lever: Map cross-section color band thickness to doneness scale; medium-well = mostly gray with only a thin pink core, distinguishing from medium (wider pink) and well-done (no pink).

seeds.scene: A magnified photo strip of 5 woven fabric swatches with the same yarn color. Visible thread counts per square cm differ: F1 dense tight weave, F2 medium weave, F3 loose open weave with visible gaps, F4 medium-tight, F5 dense with diagonal twill. A spec sheet says 'select the fabric most resistant to wind passing through.'
seeds.question: Which fabric should be selected?
seeds.lever: Wind resistance = lowest porosity = densest weave with smallest gaps; reject diagonal patterns that don't change air permeability when ranks are tied.

seeds.scene: A glass bowl contains 8 clear spherical objects sitting on a wood tabletop. Some show condensation droplets on their outer surface and a small puddle beneath; others are dry. The 8 objects: positions 1, 3, 5 wet with puddle; positions 2, 4, 6, 7, 8 dry.
seeds.question: How many of the spheres are ICE (not glass)?
seeds.lever: Ice causes condensation + meltwater puddle; glass at room temperature does neither. Count wet+puddle objects.

seeds.scene: Four bottles being poured from the same height into identical bowls; each pour stream's thickness, length-before-break, and shape differ: B1 thin continuous straight stream, B2 thick slow ribbon, B3 droplet-by-droplet, B4 medium stream. A label task: 'find the HONEY.'
seeds.question: Which bottle holds the honey?
seeds.lever: Honey = high viscosity → thick slow continuous ribbon (not dripping discretely, not thin and fast); reject fast/thin (water-like) and droplet (very thick paste-like).

seeds.scene: Six clean-looking glasses upturned on a rack under directional light. Each has subtle markers: G1 visible streaks, G2 single water spot, G3 spotless clear, G4 cloudy haze film, G5 spotless clear, G6 fingerprint smudge on rim. A note: 'reject anything with film, streaks, or smudges; spots/dots OK.'
seeds.question: How many glasses PASS the cleanliness check?
seeds.lever: Apply rule: reject film (G4), streak (G1), smudge (G6); spots OK (G2). Pass: G2, G3, G5 = 3.

seeds.scene: A produce stand with 6 round red fruits unlabeled. Visual cues: F1 has a star-shaped calyx pit (apple), F2 smooth uniform skin and small stem (tomato), F3 has slight fuzz and a crease (peach turning red), F4 has a hard glossy skin with small dimple (pomegranate), F5 has visible seeds protruding through skin (strawberry), F6 has a long thin stem and tiny size (cherry).
seeds.question: How many of the items are TRUE TOMATOES?
seeds.lever: Disambiguate by stem morphology, calyx, surface texture; only F2 matches tomato signature, others are confounders.

seeds.scene: A string of 12 incandescent bulbs photographed in dim ambient light. Some bulbs are dark filament-visible (off), some glow warm orange (on), some glow brightly white (on at full power), and one shows hairline broken filament (failed). Distribution: 5 fully white, 3 warm orange, 3 dark with intact filament, 1 dark with broken filament.
seeds.question: How many bulbs are RECEIVING POWER?
seeds.lever: Receiving power = visibly emitting light (any brightness); off filament-intact = no power; broken filament = receiving power but not glowing. Sum lit (5+3) only.

seeds.scene: A row of 5 white round plates. Each has a small chip on the rim revealing the inner material under the glaze: P1 reveals white porcelain body, P2 reveals beige plastic body, P3 reveals porcelain, P4 reveals plastic, P5 reveals stoneware (gray-tan).
seeds.question: How many plates are TRUE PORCELAIN?
seeds.lever: Identify material by chip cross-section, not glaze color; plastic and stoneware bodies disqualify.

seeds.scene: Four identical small statues photographed casting shadows on a white floor. Statue 1 shadow has a razor-sharp edge. Statue 2 shadow has a soft penumbra ~3cm. Statue 3 shadow has a wide diffuse penumbra ~10cm. Statue 4 shadow has a moderate ~5cm penumbra.
seeds.question: Which statue was lit by the LARGEST light source?
seeds.lever: Penumbra width grows with apparent light-source size at fixed distance; widest soft edge = largest source.

seeds.scene: Four propane tanks lined up outside a BBQ. Each shows a vertical condensation/frost line marking the liquid-gas boundary inside, visible as a horizontal band on the metal: T1 line near the bottom, T2 line at mid-tank, T3 line near the top, T4 no visible line.
seeds.question: Which tank has the MOST gas remaining inside?
seeds.lever: The frost line marks the top of the liquid propane; higher line = more liquid remains; no line = effectively empty.

seeds.scene: Six gray bar-shaped objects on a tray. Beside each lies a pile of identical iron filings; some piles cling and form lines along the bar (magnetic force visible as filings standing up at the ends), others sit loose. From left to right: bars 1, 3, 5 show filings stuck and standing; bars 2, 4, 6 show loose filings with no clinging.
seeds.question: How many bars are MAGNETIC?
seeds.lever: Direct visual evidence of magnetic field (filings clinging and aligning) — count only those, ignore identical-looking non-magnetic bars.

seeds.scene: Five close-up macro shots of shoe upper material. Visible grain features: S1 irregular pore pattern with scratch healing visible (real leather), S2 perfectly regular embossed pore pattern (synthetic), S3 irregular pores + visible follicle marks (real leather), S4 visible weave under coating (coated fabric), S5 regular pattern but with stitching showing real grain at edge (synthetic).
seeds.question: How many of the materials are GENUINE LEATHER?
seeds.lever: Genuine leather = irregular natural pore pattern (S1, S3); synthetic = regular embossed pattern even when convincing; coated fabric reveals weave under wear.

seeds.scene: Two side-by-side long-exposure photographs of identical-looking white eggs spinning on a table. Egg A shows a sharply defined spinning blur (spinning fast and steadily). Egg B shows wobbly motion blur and is visibly off-center, blurrier and tilting.
seeds.question: Which egg is RAW?
seeds.lever: A raw egg has fluid interior whose inertia lags rotation, causing wobble; cooked egg's solid interior spins cleanly. Wobble = raw.

seeds.scene: Four iron rods just pulled from a forge laid on an anvil. Color from tip: rod 1 dull cherry red, rod 2 bright orange, rod 3 yellow-white, rod 4 dark red barely glowing. A wall chart maps glow color to temperature: dark red ~500°C, cherry ~700°C, orange ~900°C, yellow-white ~1100°C.
seeds.question: Which rod is HOTTEST?
seeds.lever: Map blackbody glow color to temperature; yellow-white > orange > cherry > dark red.

seeds.scene: Four planks of identical-length 2x4 lumber stacked. Each shows a different deformation: cup, bow, twist, straight. A note: 'green (wet) wood arrived yesterday and was not stickered properly; mark for re-drying any plank that has warped.'
seeds.question: How many planks need to be MARKED for re-drying?
seeds.lever: Any non-flat shape (cup, bow, twist) indicates differential drying stress = needs re-drying; only the straight plank passes.

seeds.scene: Four loudspeakers sitting on a test bench, each photographed mid-playback at the same instant. Cone positions: speaker 1 cone deeply pushed inward, speaker 2 cone at rest, speaker 3 cone slightly displaced, speaker 4 cone far displaced outward.
seeds.question: Which speaker is currently producing the LOUDEST sound?
seeds.answer: speaker 1 or speaker 4 (largest displacement either direction)
seeds.lever: Loudness ∝ peak cone displacement amplitude regardless of direction; both 1 (in) and 4 (out) show maximum excursion vs the smaller and rest cones.
